impact_scope.description: The existing public hasher.update! path stops selecting the private x86 SSE4.2 implementation and uses the scalar private up! implementation unconditionally; its caller-visible signature, input, and lifecycle are unchanged.

evidence: In S0, public hasher.update!(x: roslice base.u8) already exists and accepts the same caller-supplied byte slice.
H0 enables and exercises JSON modules only and contains no xxhash32 hasher construction or update! call.
In S1, public hasher.update!(x: roslice base.u8) remains the same callable surface with the same caller-supplied byte slice.
H0 remains unchanged and still has no xxhash32 hasher construction or update! call; the removal of internal SIMD dispatch does not change how a harness reaches or controls update!.

new_harness_obligation.description: No new H0 entry point, argument, buffer, call-order transition, configuration, or special input construction is required. Exercising the affected behavior would require the same omitted hasher.update! call before and after.
evidence: The S0-to-S1 change removes choose-based private implementation dispatch and deletes a private CPU fast path.
The public update! declaration and its x argument are unchanged, while private up! remains invoked automatically by update!.

reason: For the identical public hasher.update! exposure obligation, the harness gap is true in both S0 and S1. The diff changes only the internal processing backend and introduces no concrete caller-visible harness action, so the fixed truth table yields UNCHANGED and no maintenance need.
